subject: Onramp commitments & MAP: pricing tiers and checkpoint approvals
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & onramp commitments — need pricing anchors and acceptance criteria

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is interested in moving from evaluation to a formal onramp, but we need something we can show procurement: a clear mutual action plan (MAP) with milestone acceptance criteria and the commercial levers that will kick in at each checkpoint (pricing, discounts, commit levels).

Specifically we need:
- A proposed MAP with dates and acceptance criteria for three checkpoints (POC signoff, staged ramp, production acceptance).
- A pricing worksheet that maps commit tiers to unit price and any conditional discounts tied to milestones.
- A quick SOW draft and an indication of typical legal lead time (we may need to route to procurement).

Can you share a draft this week? Also please flag any items that require executive approval (credits/discounts) so we can factor timing into our close plan.

Thanks — Sam

--
Sam Jenkins
Director, AI Infrastructure
Acme Platform
sam.jenkins@acme.com
(415) 555-0142

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & onramp commitments — need pricing anchors and acceptance criteria

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attached are two docs to start: a MAP draft (acme_MAP_v1.3.pdf) and a pricing workup (pricing_workup_ACME.xlsx). High-level proposal below; please review and tell me which acceptance criteria you want tightened/loosened.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Checkpoint 1 — POC acceptance (2–4 weeks)
   - Acceptance: 3 production-like prompts, SLA latency benchmark met, basic security questionnaire completed
   - Commercial: trial credits + baseline price tier (no commit)
2) Checkpoint 2 — Staged onramp (months 1–3)
   - Acceptance: weekly quality gates, KV-cache integration confirmed, 30% of target throughput achieved
   - Commercial: Customer commits to a 3-month ramp schedule; conditional 15% checkpoint discount if acceptance criteria met by end of month 3
3) Checkpoint 3 — Production & ramp completion (month 4+)
   - Acceptance: sustained throughput at agreed commit for 30 days, incident response SLA in place
   - Commercial: full committed-rate pricing and an additional one-time credit equal to 5% of first quarter spend if all checkpoints accepted on schedule

Pricing anchors (from pricing_workup_ACME.xlsx):
- On-demand (no commit): $0.0065 / token-equivalent unit
- 3-month staged commit (>= $100k/month run-rate by month 4): $0.0049 / unit post-commit
- Conditional checkpoint discount (Checkpoint 2 met on time): additional 15% off committed price (applied retroactively to month 2–3 usage)

Next steps I recommend:
- You confirm dates for the three checkpoints and any procurement constraints.
- We get your procurement/legal contact so I can loop in our legal and attach the SOW draft.
- If you like this structure, I’ll request an approval from our revenue ops for the conditional discount and return a redlined SOW.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme_MAP_v1.3.pdf (PDF)] [Attachment: pricing_workup_ACME.xlsx (Excel)]

Happy to hop on a 30 min call to walk through; how’s Thurs 10am PT?

— Mateo
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | (650) 555-0199

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP & onramp commitments — ACME (deal ACME-8421) — pricing concession ask

Marissa / Priyom — forwarding Sam’s request and the MAP draft. Key commercial ask: a conditional 15% discount at Checkpoint 2 if acceptance occurs on schedule. Pricing workup attached.

My suggested concession path if we want to balance risk:
- Approve up to 15% conditional discount applied retroactively months 2–3 only, on the condition Acme commits to >= $100k/month run-rate by month 4 OR a minimum annualized commitment of $1.1M within 90 days.
- Require explicit acceptance criteria and telemetry traces as proof of acceptance (we should define the QA gates in the SOW).
- Limit the one-time credit at production to 5% and tie payout to invoice cycle after acceptance period completes.

Legal contact for ACME procurement is unknown — need a PO/PO contact to speed SOW execution. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-8421

If you approve the concession path I’ll ask RevOps to sign off and prep a redlined SOW for their legal.

— Mateo

[Forwarded attachments: acme_MAP_v1.3.pdf, pricing_workup_ACME.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP & onramp commitments — ACME (deal ACME-8421) — pricing concession ask

Thanks Mateo — I’m comfortable with the proposed concession path with the following guardrails:
- Conditional discount capped at 15% and only retroactive to months 2–3 as proposed. No open-ended discounting beyond month 3.
- Require SRE/CS to validate acceptance telemetry; add a brief acceptance checklist to SOW (3 bullets max).
- Add an SLA clause (incident response time + uptime target) for production pricing to kick in.
- We can offer a small onboarding credit (up to 5% of Q1 spend) but it must be processed as a credit on the invoice after acceptance; no up-front rebate.

Priyom — can you queue RevOps for a quick approval and prepare a redline for the SOW (SOW_ACME_draft.docx) and confirm if legal will require any additional indemnity language? Ben — capture the traffic/seq expectations so we can define the commit thresholds.

If RevOps signs off I’ll send a formal commercial summary and request signature via DocuSign. Aim to have the SOW to Acme by next Tue.

— Marissa
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

1) Please send the redlined SOW and the commercial summary in one package so procurement has a single doc set.
2) We’ll need DocuSign for the final SOW + signature from our VP Procurement. We expect a 3–5 business day review window on our side.

If you can send the DocuSign link and the packet this afternoon we’ll queue it up. Proposed kickoff (post-signature): 2027-07-06 10:00am PT.

Attachments: [Attachment: Acme_PO_stub.pdf (PDF)]

Best,
Sam
